# claude-code-unity-studio

> A guide and a template to make an original Unity 6 game with Claude Code from the first idea to the release (phases
> with gates, an originality challenge against clones, the story and the script), and to run the project as a game
> studio runs production, with many parallel Claude
> Code sessions (AI coding agents) on one Mac as the team: the human as game director; a producer session (milestones
> with exit criteria, backlog, risks, reviews, merges); owner sessions as discipline leads, specialists on demand, and task sessions, in Git worktrees (APFS
> clones that cost almost no disk); one Unity runner session as build and QA engineer, with a job queue and a lock (two slots,
> a disk guard); QA with bug triage; a C# compile check without Unity; test tiers with a pre-commit hook; bot and
> network test skeletons; play reports and playtests; release candidates with one zip for each system. MIT licence.
> Tested on one game with one user for about three weeks; macOS only for the clone worktrees.

Use it when you make a Unity game with Claude Code and want more than one session at the same time, without full disks,
merge conflicts in scenes, or Unity jobs that block each other. It is not a set of agent personas, and it does not
connect Claude to the Unity Editor window (see the similar projects in the README).

## Start

- [The guide](docs/guide.md): the order of the work from the first idea to the release, the phases, the gates, who does what
- [What to avoid](docs/ai-pitfalls.md): clones, average ideas, taste given away, generic text, and the countermeasures
- [The concept phase](docs/concept-phase.md): your own ideas first, comparables, the challenger, the originality gate, key risks
- [The story and the script](docs/narrative.md): the order of the story work, the story bible, what AI does well there
- [README](README.md): what it is, the limits, the quick start, the similar projects
- [sessions.conf](sessions.conf): the one configuration file of all tools
- [setup.sh](setup.sh): makes an empty Unity 6 project with the Unity CLI and adds the samples

## Method

- [The studio model](docs/studio-model.md): roles, milestones (vertical slice, alpha, beta, release candidate), rhythm, gaps, sources
- [Roles](docs/roles.md): the human (creative director), the coordinator (producer), the runner (build and QA engineer), owners, specialists on demand, task sessions
- [The operating model](docs/operating-model.md): one contact for the human, the daily rhythm, the daily triage, session rotation with handoff files
- [The life of a session](docs/session-lifecycle.md): the steps from the brief to the final report; messages and notes
- [The merge rule](docs/merge-rule.md): team branch prefixes, pull requests, review, a merge only after the human says yes
- [More than one team](docs/multi-team.md): claims, messages, the shared board, the 11-step protocol for each coordinator
- [File ownership](docs/file-ownership.md): one owner for each file; generated files
- [Disk and worktrees](docs/disk-and-worktrees.md): the disk budget; APFS clone worktrees
- [The Unity runner](docs/unity-runner.md): one session runs Unity from a queue; the lock
- [Test tiers](docs/test-tiers.md): the compile check without Unity, the tiers, the hook, flaky tests, bots, network tests
- [The play-report loop](docs/play-report-loop.md): numbered reports, the report key, the 10-minute focus list
- [Release rules](docs/release-rules.md): one zip for each system, checks before and after the upload
- [Lessons](docs/lessons.md): what went wrong, and the fix for each problem

## Tools

- [tools/unity-lock.sh](tools/unity-lock.sh): the lock for Unity batch jobs
- [tools/quick-compile.sh](tools/quick-compile.sh): the C# compile check without Unity (about 5 s)
- [tools/new-worktree.sh](tools/new-worktree.sh): a new worktree as an APFS clone of the main checkout
- [tools/test-tier.sh](tools/test-tier.sh): the test tiers smoke, quick, full, nightly
- [tools/release.sh](tools/release.sh): the release zips, the checks, the GitHub release

## Templates

- [templates/CLAUDE.md](templates/CLAUDE.md): a CLAUDE.md for the game
- [templates/briefs/](templates/briefs/): a brief for each kind of session
- [templates/board/](templates/board/): the shared board for more than one team, its data model, and the protocol
- [templates/play-report.md](templates/play-report.md): the reading and the fixes of a human play report
- [templates/concept-challenge.md](templates/concept-challenge.md), [concept-doc.md](templates/concept-doc.md), [comparables.md](templates/comparables.md), [prototype-plan.md](templates/prototype-plan.md), [story-bible.md](templates/story-bible.md), [script-outline.md](templates/script-outline.md), [ai-record.md](templates/ai-record.md): the concept and story documents
- [templates/daily-summary.md](templates/daily-summary.md), [templates/handoff.md](templates/handoff.md): the daily summary of the coordinator, the handoff file of a rotation
- [templates/milestones.md](templates/milestones.md), [risks.md](templates/risks.md), [bugs.md](templates/bugs.md), [playtest-plan.md](templates/playtest-plan.md), [release-checklist.md](templates/release-checklist.md), [retrospective.md](templates/retrospective.md), [pillars.md](templates/pillars.md), [feature-onepager.md](templates/feature-onepager.md): the production documents
